document.abstract: A new method of color space conversion for the laser film recorder is proposed. The input image file (10 bits or more, RGB) is converted by a three-dimensional lookup table (3-D LUT), then fed to the film recorder as data from 10-bit RGB. Using this method, the image on print films is colorimetrically improved and matched to the image on a CRT monitor. This paper reviews a color transformation by conventional film recording that uses only one-dimensional LUT. A 3-D LUT is built based on a gamut mapping algorithm to compensate for the difference of the color gamut between CRT monitors and print films, employing a new soft-clipping method. Three gamut compression (clipping) methods are also evaluated. The calculation on the 3-D LUT is based on CIE LAB color coordinates evaluated by several observers. A guideline for quality control of color management in film laboratories is also discussed. This new system has been successfully applied to the production of feature animation footage.

authors.bio: Ado Ishii is a senior research and development engineer in the engineering solutions division at Imagica Corp., Tokyo, Japan, where he develops color management technologies for input and output devices for use in post-production facilities. He received a B.E. degree in electrical and information engineering from Yokohama National University, Japan, in 1987. In the same year, he joined Imagica Corp. and has since worked on hardware design of image processors for HD video and high-resolution film scanner.
